summary: [SPECULATIVE ESTIMATE] KERNEL CONTEST: The uncodified yet deeply institutionalized norms of the global order (the shared practice-norm kernel) read by status-quo powers as a neutral, universal coordination scaffold safeguarding state sovereignty and free trade versus read by revisionist powers as an un-amendable Western extraction framework designed to entrench post-Cold War hegemony. This represents a foundational macro-level authority-grounding contest.

[SPECULATIVE ESTIMATE] KERNEL CONTEST: The fixed statutory text of the 1951 Refugee Convention (the legal kernel) read restrictively by sovereign destination states to narrow definitions of 'well-founded fear' or 'particular social groups' (limiting access and maximizing domestic insulation) versus read expansively by human rights institutions as an unbendable humanitarian mandate. The contest directly alters the victim set of border enforcement[cite: 2, 3].

[SPECULATIVE ESTIMATE] KERNEL CONTEST: The codified Internet Engineering Task Force specification for TCP (the fixed protocol kernel) read by standard network clients as a strict, invariant state machine required to maintain worldwide data coordination (a pure Rope) versus read adversarially or optimization-centrically by middleboxes and specialized architectures to extract speed or surveillance capacity. A pure information-standard kernel contest[cite: 2, 3].

[SPECULATIVE ESTIMATE] KERNEL CONTEST: The formal text and structural findings of the Rogers Commission Report (the fixed historical kernel) read by engineers as an absolute technocratic safety threshold versus read by NASA administrative management as a performative compliance narrative shield designed to preserve launching velocity. Competing readings generate a severe internal authority gap[cite: 2, 3].
